svg.text: CraftBot: Physical Prototyping Through Large Language Models
Experiment 16 - Expressive Structure, GPT-6 v02 · page 2
Tall enclosure height.
about 4.1 m in front projection, at least
+/-25% uncertainty. 6.000 m clear. Deliberate brief override to
achieve exact 2:1.
Prominent front frame rhythm.
five lines / four bays. seven
transverse frames / six depth bays. Synthesis with expressive repeated
roof; not a photographic replica.
Low aperture.
no reliable absolute scale. 0.900 x 2.100 m clear.
Programme assumption for a usable entrance.
Raised floor and exterior stair.
present in reference. floor 0.096 m
above grade; no stair. Single room brief does not require raised tower
access; simple low threshold.
Experiment 16 design notes — GPT-6
2026-09-14 — v01 concept: two envelopes
The five images share a useful distinction: a calm enclosure can sit
within a much more active external assembly. Adopt a flat red square
room and put changing depth in exterior column trusses and roof
trusses. Rejected a wavy inner wall/ceiling because the brief expressly
asks for the inside to remain simple. Rejected separate decorative fins
because the exterior must read as a series of trusses with actual web
triangles and identifiable load paths.
2026-09-14 — v01 concept: scale and photo calibration
The front-photo stair supplies a weak scale anchor: about10
assumed170mm risers across280 pixels gives about165px/m at the
stair plane. That suggests roughly2.8m facade width; it does not
measure a clear room or cancel perspective. Initial3.6m width would
have added about29% to that estimate. After scope review,
adopted3.0m width (+7%, within the stated uncertainty) and
exactly6.0m clear height. Rejected a claim of surveyed dimensions.
The height is a deliberate brief-led increase over the approximate4.1m
projected photo enclosure. The user ratio is the controlling dimension.
The reference's low opening is not credible as a normal-door
calibration. A0.9x2.1m opening provides one usable entrance. Raised
floor and exterior staircase from the red tower are not copied:
a0.096m slat-mat floor keeps the requested single room direct and
compact. No second entrance, movable door leaf, stair or gallery has
been added.
2026-09-14 — v01 concept: thin slats and load paths
The repeated catalogue is24x90mm boarding and36x90mm
structural slats. Paired chords bracket a single web layer; deep truss
action comes from separated chords, not a solid thick beam. Roof
reactions go to the paired side-column heads, down triangulated
inner/outer chords to sole runners and a crossed slat mat. Longitudinal
braces tie frame stations to ground; explicit floor/roof diagonals
collect lateral action. Rejected conventional glulam posts, plywood
gussets and steel brackets as modeled elements because they would
undermine the entirely-thin-timber brief. Concealed fasteners and
anchors are acknowledged as unresolved construction necessities.
The manuals establish only analogies: CMHC19mm boards
at600mm support spacing and FRIM35x72mm truss members
over5.77m. Our24mm boards at500mm spacing and36x90 paired
chords are mine, not manual-certified. The6m braced columns,
connections, base anchors and soil interface have no matching
prescriptive design. No structural adequacy claim is made.
2026-09-14 — v01 concept: fixed faceted expression
Seven frames at500mm spacing carry an additive roof height field:
a low curved profile sampled across x plus a changing vertical offset
along y. Each interval remains a planar facet, so straight short slats
can close the roof and bear at their ends. The outer side-column nodes
also vary in depth while their inner chords stay vertical. Rejected an
arbitrary double-curved skin that would force twisted long boards;
rejected a simple pitched roof repeated unchanged because the two
expressive references ask for stronger articulation.
All characteristic profiles and paired chord layer offsets are fixed in
concept.md before geometry. A Builder may fit and clip joints within
those profiles; changing the room, number of ribs, exterior expression
or member catalogue is a design question.
2026-09-14 — v01 concept: enclosure and daylight
scope
Opaque lower walls concentrate light at0.75m-high clerestory
bands immediately under the6m ceiling on both side walls. End walls
remain full-height red boards, as in the interior photo. The roof is
fully covered by slats and ceiling is a level slat plane. No glass or
membrane is modeled. CraftBot confirmed the open-air pavilion
reading on2026-09-14: this is a geometric architectural proposal with
no demonstrated rain-tightness or conditioned-building performance.
Rejected adding glazing merely to make the model appear
weatherproof.
Deviation ledger at concept release
Category. Decision. Reason / rejected alternative.
Source deviation.
3.0x3.0x6.0m clear volume. Photo width
estimate retained approximately; exact user2:1 ratio overrides
projected photo height.
Source deviation.
Seven transverse frames rather than copying five
prominent front lines. Series synthesizes roof references; red photos
guide scale and assembly, not a literal replica.
Source deviation.
Usable0.9x2.1m entrance; floor close to grade.
No requirement for low aperture or raised tower stair.
Source deviation.
All-slat paired nodes instead of FRIM plywood
gussets and steel base shoes. User material palette; connection
capacity not inferred from substituted detail.
Considered, kept.
Red vertical enclosure, natural chords,
triangulated webs, high side light. Features agree across the
red-building and expressive references.
Considered, kept.
Level inner ceiling despite varying roof trusses.
Expressive exterior must not disturb simple interior.
Not verified.
Strength, buckling, fasteners, uplift/overturning, soil
bearing, moisture, fire, weatherproofing. Outside source coverage and
geometric checks; no construction certification.
Phase-2 comparison and structural review
Performed on v02 on 2026-09-15. The comparison and
structural-review records below supersede the concept-stage
placeholder. The original concept decisions and v01 clarification
remain as the design history.
2026-09-14 — v01 build clarification: sole-runner
datum
Accepted the Builder's integrated upper-layer sole runner assembly.
Continuous longitudinal S runners occupy z=-0.060..-0.024, and
upper transverse sleeper segments stop at their faces. Column feet
remain at z=-0.024. Lower longitudinal sleepers sit directly beneath
the runners and every foot footprint, carrying the load from foot to
runner to lower sleeper to grade without a thin-slat cantilever. Floor
support spacing remains <=0.500 m; fitted butt contacts replace
intersecting volumes, with concealed connection design still
unverified. This clarifies R-16 and the SOLE_RUNNERS row
without changing stock or clear room dimensions.
Rejected placing a third 36 mm sole layer above the mat because it
would raise feet to z=+0.012 and contradict the released COLUMN_Z
datum. Rejected omitting the runner because a continuous bearing and
tying line is part of the stated base assembly. The accepted
arrangement retains that line within the existing 96 mm
ground-to-floor stack; the crossing mat is continuous through the
lower layer where upper transverse pieces are interrupted.
2026-09-15 — v02 independent structural review
This review concerns the built evidence in version_notes.md
v01/v02, inspection_v01.md, inspection_v02.md and
inspection_v02_room.md. The Designer did not read the geometry
scripts or renders, and did not infer compliance merely from the
concept. The Builder supplies numerical and fitted-plane evidence;
the room Inspector supplies the separate visual channel. The reference
images were set aside for this pass.
Element family / condition. Built load-path argument and evidence.
Finding / action.
Roof slats.
Version notes report short boards spanning adjacent
0.500 m frame stations with undersides on the actual beveled
upper-chord planes and fitted facet boundaries. Inspector views 11/16
show complete coverage and support lines. Gravity goes through
those contacts to the upper chords. Retain R-15. No reported
unsupported board or visible gap. Every contact area is not
independently measurable in renders; no roof-board capacity or
fastening claim.
Roof trusses.
Notes identify upper/lower chords, web nodes,
column-head seats and complementary joints; views 08/11/12 confirm
web triangles and supported heels. Reactions pass through the
web/chord assembly to the paired inner and outer column heads.
Retain R-08/R-17/R-22. The 90 mm seats are Builder evidence,
visually consistent at view 12. Connection forces and the adequacy of
segmented chord splices remain undesigned.
Ceiling.
Notes explicitly put ceiling top at z = 6.024 against the
lower-chord underside. Its gravity load goes through concealed face
fixings into the lower chords, then to column heads. View 19
confirms a level unobstructed plane. Retain R-23. This is a proposed
fixing-dependent load path, not bearing from above. Fixing number,
withdrawal resistance and fire performance are unverified.
Side and end-wall boards / rails.
Notes report rails at no more
than 0.750 m, supported staggered board joints, ripped side
attachment battens and end rails terminating at inner-chord faces.
Boards transfer gravity and out-of-plane loads through their fixings
and rails to exterior chords; lower board ends also meet the floor edge
where detailed. Views 06/07/10/19 confirm the enclosure and upper
openings. Retain R-05/R-21. Exact rail spacing and every concealed
attachment depend on Builder evidence; no wall shear capacity is
assigned to the boarding.
Entrance discontinuity.
Notes name a header with 90 mm seats,
doubled jamb plies, a ripped edge slat supporting both plies, and
removed infill/rails inside the passage. The header carries infill above
into the jambs, then into the supported mat edge. The transverse roof
frames avoid using this opening as their principal roof support. View
15 confirms the header/jamb grammar and clear passage. Retain
R-02/R-18. No uncarried end or obstructing member is reported.
Header, jamb and connection capacities remain uncalculated.
Truss-column feet and soles.
v02 actual-mesh assertion checks all
56 horizontal foot faces against both sole and lower sleeper, including
support top levels and full 90.000 mm seat width. The sole is at z =
-0.060..-0.024, the aligned lower sleeper at z = -0.096..-0.060, then
grade. View 14 shows seated feet. R-16 is resolved geometrically.
The former maximum 0.753 mm unsupported edge per side was
removed by fitted foot-end bevels, not hidden by a relaxed tolerance.
No further strips or larger stock justified.
Floor and ground mat.
Notes report floor boards spanning the
0.500 m stations, upper transverse sleeper pieces fitted against
continuous longitudinal sole runners, and lower sleepers directly
below column-foot lines. Floor gravity passes to upper
sleepers/runners, then the lower layer, then grade. Views 09/18 show
continuous support and no isolated floor strip. Retain R-14/R-16. No
modeled retaining wall, slope or suspended undercroft requires
another foundation detail. Soil pressure, settlement and long-term
timber-to-grade exposure are unverified.
Transverse x direction.
Each x-z roof/column frame contains
actual triangles. Roof-plane braces collect lateral action over the room
width to the exterior truss-column lines; the frame chord/web forces
reach their separated feet and the mat. Frame view 08 and
roof-bracing view 17 confirm the relevant members. Retain
R-08/R-20. This is a braced truss proposal, not a moment frame.
Global resistance still depends on designed node connections and
ground hold-downs; contact alone cannot carry tension or
overturning.
Longitudinal y direction.
Built notes identify longitudinal ties at
column nodes and diagonal end bays connecting the seven frames.
The nominal 3.0 m frame array has 0.500 m bays. Roof/ground-plan
diagonals collect shear into these braced side lines, whose braces
continue to the mat. Views 07/08/17/18 confirm the members. Retain
R-19/R-20. Fitted tie/brace ends were segmented to avoid
intersections in v01; their force continuity requires concealed
fasteners, which are named but not designed. Skin is not claimed as
the diaphragm.
Member slenderness and restraint.
The reported system remains
36 x 90 mm structural slats, paired for chords, with roughly 1.5 m
column panels and 0.500 m frame repetition. A single 36 mm ply has
a weak-axis radius of gyration of 36/sqrt(12) = 10.4 mm; if a 1.5 m
panel were an effective buckling length, L/r would be about 144. This
is the Designer's dimensional indicator, not a stability calculation;
paired-ply composite action and effective restraint are not established.
Keep the explicit unsupported-engineering finding in R-26/R-28. The
slender column system needs member, restraint and connection
design before construction. No evidence supports an arbitrary larger
post or a change to the thin-slat brief during this geometric review.
Sliding, uplift, moisture and drainage.
Notes do not model a
ground anchor, moisture break or weatherproof membrane. The roof
is faceted and fully covered with slats; upper clerestories are
intentionally open. A seated foot transmits compression but does not
establish a tensile ground connection. Roof seams/falls have no
demonstrated waterproof drainage detail. Record as unverified under
R-28, not as proven stability or weather protection. No glazed
enclosure, steel shoe, concrete foundation or membrane is silently
added. This remains the accepted conceptual pavilion scope.
The two reported geometric checks are 0 penetrating pairs above 1
mm and 0 floating members at a 2 mm contact tolerance, with no
exclusions. They neither prove global connectivity to ground nor
adequate bearing by themselves. The separate v02 full-foot assertion
uses actual horizontal mesh faces and a 1 micrometre precision
tolerance; it supplies the specific bearing evidence missing from v01.
Roof and doorway seats use Builder dimension/assembly evidence
with visual consistency, not an equally comprehensive independent
mesh-bearing audit.
No new geometric defect is established by this review. The explicit
lateral members, full-foot correction and documented opening/support
paths meet the geometric requirements without another version. This
conclusion is limited to the supplied built records and Inspector
findings. It does not certify that the pavilion is stable, anchored,
weatherproof or ready to construct. R-14/R-15/R-21/R-22/R-23 retain
their stated partial-visibility limits; those limitations are not waived
visible defects.
Rejected unnecessary changes: added base strips would duplicate
the resolved foot bearing; a third sole layer would change the
accepted datum; oversized posts or plywood gussets would replace
the user's thin-slat system without an engineering design; glazing or a
membrane would expand the accepted pavilion scope. None is
introduced as a speculative fix.
2026-09-15 — v02 source-versus-model comparison
and final design disposition
The mechanical comparison Inspector opened all five original input
photographs, the six concept-cited manual snippets, and v02 views
01–04, 06–08 and 10–19. Its complete row-by-row record is
inspection_v02_comparison.md. The following Designer table
accepts or acts on those actual-image findings; it is not a comparison
inferred from the concept text. No additional source search was
undertaken.
Reference image / figure. In the reference. In v02, from comparison
Inspector. Change or retained with reason.
01-soane-front.jpg.
Tall compact red volume in thin framing; five
prominent front lines, raised floor and exterior stair. Views 03/06
show the red volume, pale/red frame and centered entry; the
seven-frame rhythm is along depth. Retain. A 3.0 m room width is
close to the approximate 2.8 m photograph estimate. The 6.0 m height
deliberately overrides the approximate 4.1 m photo height to meet the
user's exact 2:1 ratio. Seven depth frames and a low threshold are
recorded synthesis choices.
02-soane-outside.jpg.
Paired slender timber, diagonal braces, open
gaps and small projections around red boarding. Views 01–04/07/08
show paired pale members, red webs, repeated projections and open
structural depth. Retain. This is the strongest direct
construction-character transfer. Projections are not literal survey
dimensions; no heavy post substitute appears.
03-soaneinterior-1.jpg.
Tall red vertical boards, high side light,
simple floor and unusually low aperture. Views 06/10/19 show the
tall clear room, level ceiling and upper side openings with the normal
entrance. Retain. Usable 0.9 x 2.1 m entry and a flat ceiling preserve
the programme. View 19 hides end boards to expose construction, so
the enclosure comparison also uses view 10 and front view 06; it is
not a photometric daylight test.
Erne_Dachbau_778.webp.
Repeated segmented trusses with
genuine triangles and changing depth. Views 01–04/08/11/16 show a
compact series of triangulated roof ribs, changing profile and slat
cover. Retain. The truss system is adapted to the pavilion's scale. Its
industrial dimensions and joint capacities are not transferred.
Tchumi-02.jpg.
Repeated straight members describe a
rising/falling projected outer profile; glass behind a dense timber
screen. Views 01–04/07/08 show a side wave from straight slats with
layered depth and shadow. Retain. The outer articulation is
transferred; glass, dense screening, vegetation and optical
performance are outside the adopted brief.
FRIM Sheet 9 truss elevation / heel.
Slender triangular truss with
heel supports and center rise. Views 08/11/12 show changing-depth
roof triangles and lower-chord seats on paired column heads. Retain
topology and supported heel. Faceting, span and paired nodes are
project-specific rather than a scaled structural design.
FRIM Sheet 9 roof-bracing plan.
Roof-plane diagonals restrain
and tie the truss series. Views 08/17 show longitudinal ties and
crossed diagonal pairs connecting the seven frames. Retain. Apparent
crossings in projected images are not an identified solid penetration;
the separate geometry report remains zero pairs. Brace joint capacity
is unverified.
FRIM Sheet 9 gussets / nailing.
Plywood gussets and specified
nail patterns transfer node forces. Views 12/13 show layered timber
contacts and straps without gussets or hardware. Retain as the explicit
all-slat deviation. This does not establish that the substituted node can
develop the source truss forces; fastening must be designed.
CMHC Fig. 68 wall opening.
Lintel and jamb framing carry
interrupted wall infill. Views 06/15/19 show the supported entrance
header and jambs with infill above. Retain opening grammar. The
Builder reports 90 mm seats; the render cannot independently
measure all bearing areas or verify connections.
CMHC Fig. 86 rafter heel.
Roof members seat over aligned
supports. Views 11/12/16 show roof lower-chord seats at the
side-column heads and the level ceiling below. Retain aligned bearing
logic. The proposed truss does not adopt rafter/collar-tie prescriptions.
Ceiling gravity still requires the named face fixings.
CMHC Fig. 47 sleeper on slab.
Supported timber sleeper with
separate ground/moisture layers. Views 14/18 show the crossed slat
mat and continuous sole runners. Retain geometric bearing
arrangement, with no claim that the omitted slab, moisture break or
anchorage is supplied by wood-to-ground contact.
Disposition: all five primary photo rows and all six cited
manual-figure rows are retained or intentionally synthesized with the
reasons above. No concrete missing member, unintended envelope
gap, obstructed opening, wrong profile or other geometric/photo
defect was identified. R-13 is checked, bringing requirements to 28 of
28 without waivers. Phase 2 accepts v02 unchanged; another
geometry version would have no review finding to resolve.
Incidental specification correction: the existing roof formula
samples seven ribs at three repeated vertical offset levels through one
rise and fall. The earlier phrase "seven distinct rib heights" overstated
what that formula says. The phrase is corrected in concept.md; the
formula, dimensions and built geometry are unchanged.
Review cost evidence: one gpt-5.6-luna comparison Inspector, five
primary photos, six manual snippets and seventeen v02 render views.
This Designer reviewed built notes and reports without opening
scripts or renders. No additional renders, manual research, geometry
files or shared-tool changes were made during this phase. Token and
monetary totals are not exposed and are not estimated.
Experiment 16 version notes — GPT-6
Implemented the released 3.000 × 3.000 × 6.000 m clear room with
one 0.900 × 2.100 m entrance, two open high clerestories, flat red
vertical boarding and a level timber ceiling. Seven transverse frames
carry paired pale timber chords, red web triangles, varying
outer-column profiles and a fully boarded faceted roof. The geometry
starts from tools/experiment_template.py and uses craftbot_lib,
geometry2d, planes and framing; no shared toolkit was changed.
The crossed ground mat includes the Designer-approved continuous
sole runners within its upper layer, z=-0.060..-0.024. Transverse
sleepers butt to those runners, with lower longitudinal sleepers
directly below their centerlines. A ripped edge slat carries both
entrance-jamb plies. The doorway header has 90 mm seats. Side-wall
rails are ripped to the specified 31 mm attachment gap; end rails
terminate against the inner-chord faces. Wall butt joints stagger on
rail heights and individual wall boards are at most 3.000 m long.
Column-chord turns use complementary mitres. Roof chords are
split at web nodes; their upper faces bevel to the additive roof facets.
Short B roof boards span adjacent 0.500 m frame stations and meet on
complementary vertical facet boundaries. Ceiling boards are
face-fixed to the lower chords: concealed fixings carry their gravity
load; the boards do not bear on the tops of members above them.
Longitudinal ties and end-bay diagonals connect the transverse
frames. Roof-plan crossed braces occupy separate 36 mm layers
between the lower-chord faces. Ground-plan diagonals fit between the
crossed sleeper network in its two thickness layers. These members
name the lateral load path; boarding alone is not called a diaphragm,
and the concealed connections remain undesigned.
Verification
Final rendered model:
2,101 members, 0 penetrating pairs >1
mm, 0 floating members at 2 mm contact tolerance, 0 overlap
families.
No ignored contact families and no changed check tolerances.
Initial unrendered preflight: 2,031 members, 86 pairs, 0 floating.
Its two causes were longitudinal ties crossing column rungs (70
pairs) and longitudinal diagonals crossing transverse column webs
(16 pairs). Fitting these members to the web faces removed both
causes; the segmented ties add 70 members. Both preflights
occurred before the first render, so there is only one rendered v01.
Script assertions check clear room and entrance volumes against
every member's bounds, exact room ratio, frame spacing/count,
clerestory limit, roof-facet count, declared catalogue/material, floor
support spacing, sole/support centerline alignment, header seats
and rail spacing.
The full renderer ran successfully in Blender 4.3.2; all views
were rendered. Views include four orbits, top/front/east elevations,
frame-only, from below, room section, roof profile, heel, layered
column node, base, entrance, roof boarding, roof-plan bracing, mat
underside and interior front.
Saved model: experiment_16_gpt6_v01_blender.blend; pair report:
experiment_16_gpt6_v01_blender_pairs.txt. The version is
immutable after these renders.
Closeout's textual view-schema check initially missed the valid
frame-only view because it recognizes only a double-quoted inline
hide list or a variable named COVER. View 08's identical hide
values were inlined using double quotes; camera, visibility and
rendered view identity did not change. No rerender was necessary.
Bearing audit beyond the contact check
R-16 remains open.
A horizontal cut through each sloping
outer-column foot produces a horizontal width of
against the 90.000 mm sole/support width. The maximum
unsupported edge is
0.753 mm on each side.
The contact check
correctly reports contact but cannot prove full footprint bearing. The
next version must add adjacent ripped S sole/lower-support strips
with fitted transverse-mat cuts, or fit a local foot-end bevel within the
S stock. Preserve the released column profile, mat datums and
clear-room dimensions.
Inspection and requirements
The fresh single-room Inspector reviewed all 19 views and reported
no clear major missing geometry, unintended envelope void,
misplaced member or floating member. The room, entrance, upper
light, seven frames, layered chords and expressive roof are visually
confirmed. Detailed observations are in inspection_v01_room.md; the
merged result and Builder dispositions are in inspection_v01.md.
R-14, R-15, R-21, R-22 and R-23 contain details that cannot be
measured or seen fully in these renders. Their generation rules,
dimension chains, fitted-plane construction and named ceiling face
fixing supply the Builder evidence; there is no contrary visual finding.
The requirement checkboxes now record
26 of 28 satisfied:
awaits phase-2 reference comparison, and R-16 remains open. Thus
phase 1 is not converged.
No other visual correction was requested
for v02.
Scope and evidence limits
CMHC board-thickness examples and the FRIM slender-truss
drawing are precedents, not capacity evidence for this assembly. The
6 m slat columns are outside the cited prescriptive stud cases; FRIM
plywood gussets do not validate the modeled paired-slat joints. No
plywood, metal shoes, glazing, concrete or invented heavy beams are
modeled. The low threshold replaces the reference stair, the usable
doorway replaces its unusually low aperture, and the exact 2:1 clear
height follows the user's brief.
This is a pavilion with open high clerestories. Structural adequacy,
fastener and connection design, uplift/overturning anchorage,
weatherproofing, durability, fire, soil bearing and moisture separation
are not verified. Sections are plausible visual propositions, not
calculated. These limitations do not waive geometric bearing or
inspection findings.
Next version and Designer questions
Correct the quantified R-16 foot-seat deficit with an in-catalogue
local assembly detail; the two alternatives above preserve the
design. No scope change is requested.
No additional visual defects were identified. Recheck the base
close-up, full numeric model and required full phase-ending views
in a fresh v02; do not overwrite v01.
No open design-authority question at this stage. Usage/context
statistics are not exposed to this Builder and are not estimated.
v02 — phase 1 foot-bearing correction, 2026-09-14
Copied the immutable v01 script and corrected R-16 with fitted
foot-end bevels. Each sloping first chord segment has two additional
cut planes: they run from the edges of the 90 mm horizontal seat to
the original stock edges 90 mm above that seat. Above this short end
detail the original chord profile remains. The cuts remove material
from the S36x90 blank, keep every solid convex, and retain the fixed
column centerlines, room dimensions, sole runners and ground-mat
datums. No support strips or other members were added. The
alternative of adjacent ripped supports would require new mat cuts
and more pieces; the fitted bevel resolves the local deficit directly.
Verification
2,101 members; 0 penetrating pairs >1 mm; 0 floating
members at 2 mm contact tolerance; 0 overlap families.
No
ignored members or changed harness tolerances.
A new assertion selects the four actual mesh vertices of each
horizontal chord foot and checks that its full rectangle lies within
both the sole-runner and lower-sleeper footprint. It also checks the
support top levels and requires a full 90 mm seat. The 1
micrometre assertion tolerance accommodates Blender mesh
precision; it is distinct from the overlap/contact tolerances.
Test-first evidence: before the bevel was added, that assertion
failed on ColumnOuter_-1_00_-1_00 against SoleRunner_00.
After the correction, all
56 foot faces
passed, with measured
widths
The previous maximum 0.753 mm
unsupported edge is removed.
Full Blender 4.3.2 render completed with exit code 0; every stable
view
was rendered. No view definition changed. The base is
shown by views 14 and 18, with frame and underside context in 08
and 09.
Artifacts: experiment_16_gpt6_v02.py,
experiment_16_gpt6_v02_blender.blend,
experiment_16_gpt6_v02_blender_pairs.txt, and 19
experiment_16_gpt6_v02_blender_view_XX.png renders. No
changes to v01 geometry or shared tools were made by this
Builder. Runner owns viewer export and close-out.
Inspection and requirements
The fresh single-room Inspector completed all 19 views and found
no missing member, unintended envelope gap, clearly floating
member or new absence. Base view 14 shows seated feet without a
visible gap; the small bevel itself is below reliable visual
measurement, so the full-foot assertion supplies the exact support
evidence. Frame, underside, heel, node, roof-board and bracing views
show no regressions. Its saved report inspection_v02_room.md was
complete before the final-message usage interruption; the
continuation on 2026-09-15 merged it into inspection_v02.md
without repeating renders or inspection.
R-16 is now checked.
27 of 28 requirements are satisfied, and
phase 1 is converged:
0 pairs, 0 floating, no open visual defect, and
every phase-one requirement satisfied. R-13 alone remains pending
for phase-2 reference comparison. Runner's closeout_v02.md records
8 passed, 0 failed,
including exported model, layers, all 19 renders
and viewer screenshot.
Scope and Designer questions
The named load path remains chord foot → continuous upper sole
→ directly aligned lower sleeper → grade. Full geometric bearing is
verified; fastener forces, buckling, capacity, anchorage, soil/moisture
design and weatherproofing remain unverified. The open clerestory
pavilion and all v01 scope interpretations remain in force. Sections
are a visual proposition, not calculated.
No open design-authority question. No shared helper promotion is
proposed. Usage/context statistics are not exposed to this Builder and
are not estimated.
Credits
The project author is Luka Piškorec, previously a lecturer at Aalto
University and researcher at ETH Zürich, co-founder of TEN Studio
(Zürich and Belgrade) and {protocell:labs} (Helsinki), practices that
work at an intersection of architecture, design, digital art and
research. CraftBot is part of the art-ai-fact initiative funded by Aalto
University in 2025-2026.
